newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: TENNIS-BUSINESS AS USUAL AS PLAYERS RETURN TO CLAY.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-BUSINESS AS USUAL AS PLAYERS RETURN TO CLAY.

text.p: Spain's Felix Mantilla and South Africa's Wayne Ferreira both won their first round matches at the Swiss Open as the European clay court season resumed on Monday.
Sixth seed Mantilla, a finalist a year ago, cruised past Argentina's Lucas Arnold 7-5 6-1.
Number eight Ferreira, the only other seed to see action on the opening day, needed three sets to dispose of Spain's Francisco Clavet 3-6 6-4 6-4.
The top seeds, including number one Yevgeny Kafelnikov of Russia and number two Alex Corretja of Spain, appear on Tuesday.
Kafelnikov, the 1996 French Open champion, faces a difficult first test in 1992 Olympic champion Marc Rosset of Switzerland, who will be playing in front of a home crowd.
Corretja, winner of two tournaments already this year in Estoril and Rome, begins his quest for a third against Czech Jiri Novak.
Cedric Pioline, who became the first Frenchman since 1946 to reach the Wimbledon final, will also be hoping to make a smooth transition from grass to clay.He faces compatriot Fabrice Santoro.
